newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SPANISH FEDERATION OPPOSES BOSMAN BENEFIT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPANISH FEDERATION OPPOSES BOSMAN BENEFIT.

text.p: The Spanish Football Federation has refused to authorise a benefit game planned to be played in Barcelona on behalf of Marc Bosman, the Belgian whose test case at the European Union brought about the end of quotas on foreign players.

"The Federation thinks that the Bosman case has damaged the Spanish game...and the national team. We won't authorise the game, and we won't send a referee," said Federation press secretary Fernando Garrido on Friday.
Over 200 hundred foreigners now play in the Spanish league in the wake of the decision to lift the limit on the number of EU players per team.
"Football is a business enterprise, but we consider it to be a special case, the way that the EU recognises other areas, like the environment, to be special cases," said Garrido.
He said the game could not take place unless authorised by the Federation.
Garrido refused to be drawn on measures that could be taken against anyone invovled in an unauthorised match.
